name: Numerical Algorithms for High Performance Computing
description:
The lecture discusses selected algorithms from the following classical problem settings in scientific computing ("the seven dwarfs of HPC"), in particular:
- Solvers for partial differential equations (and related problems) on structured and unstructured grids (e.g. domain decomposition methods)
- Algorithms in numerical linear algebra on sparse and dense matrices (direct and iterative solution of linear systems on HPC architectures, eigenvalue problems, etc.)

A particular focus is on situations, where parallelisation of sequential algorithms is not sufficient, but algorithmic improvements are required to reach best-possible performance.

In that context, the following approaches for optimisation and analysis of algorithms will be discussed:
- Performance analysis and performance models (Roofline, Cache, Bulk Synchronous Parallelism) 
- Shared-memory parallelism (data dependencies, parallel loop, tasking)
- Distributed-memory parallelism (MPI; tiling, blocking and partitioning methods)
prerequisites:
IN0019 Numerical Programming, IN2156 Numerical Programming (CSE), IN2147 Parallel Programming; 
preferrably also Scientific Computing 1&2 (IN2005, IN2141) or similar courses
